reasons: Party mapping is correct: IBM is the customer/buyer and MSL the supplier, so the assignment direction in 13.1 (MSL assigns all IP in Products and inventions to IBM) runs in our favour and meets the preferred position.

Section 13.3(a) confirms no grant of IBM pre-existing IP to MSL beyond a narrow royalty-free use right solely to manufacture for IBM, and IBM-paid tooling remains IBM property (p1105) — no assignment of our IP/data to the vendor, no joint ownership, so no walk-away or fallback failure exists.

Consistent with a compliant claim, no redline or counterparty comment was produced and the deterministic check ('no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains') passes; the paragraphs are unchanged.

The rationale properly notes the only shortfalls (no express perpetual licence-back of MSL embedded pre-existing IP, no separately labelled Customer Data ownership sentence) as immaterial sub-elements rather than flagging them as deviations, which matches the playbook's classification semantics.
